numberOfTests.description: the number of test vectors in this test

HpkeEncapTestGroup.description: HPKE base-mode encapsulation (SetupBaseS), validating the recipient encapsulation key pkRm. Each group fixes one (KEM, KDF, AEAD) ciphersuite. Given pkRm and the ephemeral seed ikmE, an implementation deserializes pkRm and runs SetupBaseS, then Seal(pt, aad). For valid cases it MUST succeed and (deterministically) reproduce enc and ct; when skRm is present the sealed message also opens to pt. For invalid cases the encapsulation key is malformed and deserialization and/or SetupBaseS MUST fail (an HPKE EncapError), surfaced at key import or at encapsulation. The reject reason depends on the KEM: an ML-KEM key (draft-ietf-hpke-pq) fails the encapsulation-key check (FIPS 203 Section 7.2) or has the wrong length; a DHKEM(X25519) key that yields an all-zero Diffie-Hellman shared secret is rejected because RFC 9180 Section 5.1.1 requires DH to abort on an all-zero output, or it has the wrong length.

comment.description: A brief description of the test case

pkRm.description: The recipient encapsulation key under test (the subject of the test). For invalid cases this is malformed.

ikmE.description: Optional. The sender's encapsulation randomness (32 bytes for ML-KEM). Present for valid cases, where deterministic encapsulation reproduces enc and ct. Absent for invalid cases.

skRm.description: Optional. The recipient private key (64-byte d || z seed) corresponding to pkRm, when one exists. Present lets a consumer additionally decapsulate enc and open ct to recover pt.

info.description: The HPKE info string bound into the key schedule

aad.description: The additional authenticated data passed to Seal

pt.description: The plaintext sealed for valid cases; empty for invalid cases

enc.description: The KEM encapsulated key produced by SetupBaseS for valid cases; empty for invalid cases

ct.description: The AEAD sealed message (ciphertext || tag) for valid cases; empty for invalid cases
